title: A closed Ricci flow with bounded scalar curvature and finite-time curvature blowup
abstract: We disprove the scalar-curvature extension conjecture in its unrestricted all-dimensions form. In sufficiently high dimension, we construct a Ricci flow on a closed manifold whose scalar curvature remains uniformly bounded while full curvature diverges at a finite maximal time. In one fixed sufficiently high dimension, the examples have two-sided power-law curvature blowup with arbitrarily large exponents.
result_title: Scalar curvature and finite-time Ricci-flow singularities
subject: Differential geometry
overall_assessment:
The paper claims a Ricci flow on $\mathbb{S}^2\times\mathbb{S}^{q+1}$, for large $q$, with bounded scalar curvature and $\max_M|\mathrm{Rm}|\to\infty$ at a finite time $T$. It takes a singular flow from Stolarski's construction (Proposition 2.1) and proves new curvature estimates for it.

I recomputed the estimates that the paper proves itself and found no error. This includes the warping equations and the equations for $u$, $v$ and $r_s$; the formula for $r^2R$ and its value $-m(m-1)z$ plus the ratio term at $f=1$; the pole-orbit bound $c\theta\le\phi(0,t)\le C\theta$; the cap slope barrier $r/\theta$; the moving-cylinder inclusions and coefficient bounds; the reaction matrix and its largest eigenvalue $q-1+C\sqrt q$ after multiplication by $r^2$; the barrier $H=\delta^L(r^2+b_0\theta^2)^{-a/2}$ with $\mathcal{D}H/H\ge -L/\delta+(a(q-1)-a^2z)/D_0$; the lateral exponent $(a-d)/2>0$; the exponent $e=a-d+d/k\in(0,1)$; the scalar barrier $C_1-C_2r^{2-2e}+\varepsilon r^{-1}$; the exterior barrier $1-b_1\delta/r^2$; and the two-sided rate $\theta^{-2}=(T-t)^{-2k/d_q}$.

All the risk is in Proposition 2.1, which has a source map and no proof. Two parts are major gaps: the inner inequalities come from inside a source proof and are not shown for the selected flow, and the paper changes the initial family of the source without a new proof of the degree argument. A third part is a moderate gap: the constant $C_0$, and thus the choice of $q$ by $\mathfrak m>0$, needs the freedom to enlarge $Y_1$ and $Y_2$ after the tolerances. Two minor issues are the missing time range of the profile bounds and the unconditional wording of the abstract.

Seven of the ten sub-agent reviews returned no findings. I could not read the source memoir in this run, so the review reports these gaps as unverified dependencies, not as proven errors. The result is correct if Proposition 2.1 holds as stated.

comments.explanation:
Proposition 2.1(iv) is not a statement of the source. The paper derives it: it sets the bound on the lower-mode coefficients at the initial time to $\epsilon_0\delta^
u$ with small $\epsilon_0$, and says in one sentence that this agrees with the degree argument of Lemma 3.10 of the source. One part is correct. The lower $U$-modes are $\gamma^{-d}$ times polynomials in $\gamma^2$ of degree below $k$, thus each mode and its first two derivatives is at most $C_{q,k}(\gamma^{-d-j}+\gamma^{2k-d})$ on $\gamma>0$. The gap is the existence step. In a degree argument the size of the initial coefficient ball is not free. The map from the coefficients to the unstable projections at the exit time must have degree one onto the boundary of the trapping box. If the ball has radius $\epsilon_0\delta^
u$, the box must become smaller by the same factor. Then each error that the source compares with the box size (nonlinear terms, cutoff errors, projection errors, the inner gluing) must be small compared with $\epsilon_0$. The paper names only the projection errors of Lemmas 6.13--6.14. comments.explanation: I recomputed the comparison. With $w=\widetilde U$, the ratio identity and $(p-1)r^2/\phi^2=(q-1)e^{-2w}$ give $(\partial_t-\Delta)w=\frac{q-1}{r^2}(1-e^{-2w})$. The right side is $c\,w$ with $c$ bounded on $\{r\ge\Gamma_0\sqrt\delta\}$ on each compact time slab, so the linear maximum principle keeps $w\ge 0$. The structure is correct. The gap is in the hypothesis. The equilibrium $w=0$ is unstable, because the reaction is negative for $w<0$. Thus the argument needs $\widetilde U(\Gamma_0,t)\ge 0$ on the lateral boundary for each $t\in[0,T)$, not only for late $t$. This needs the first profile estimate with $j=0$ at $\gamma=\Gamma_0$ at all times, the tolerance condition $\eta_0^U<c_2$ up to a fixed factor, and $Y_1\delta^{\nu/d}\le\Gamma_0\le M_0e^{\beta\tau}$ from $\tau_0$ on. Proposition 2.1(ii) states the profile bounds with no time range, item (iii) is only for "sufficiently late times", and item (iv) is only for the initial time. If the bounds hold only at late times, a negative value of $w$ can enter through the boundary at an early time, and the sign does not come back. The global bound $\phi/r\ge c_0$ is used on the full interval $[0,t_i]$ in the record-point argument of Lemma 4.2, so it sets $D_1$ and $C_*$ in Proposition 5.3. The proof also increases the starting time of the construction, and this step must be put before the flow is fixed in Section 6.1. The repair is probably easy: state in Proposition 2.1(ii) that the bounds hold for all $\tau\ge\tau_0$. With that statement Theorem 1.1 is not affected.

comments.explanation: The proof of Proposition 2.1 is a source map, not a proof. Three parts of the proposition are not literal statements of the source: the inner inequalities for the selected flow, the changed initial family with bounds up to $G_{\mathrm{init}}$, and the order of choices with no upper limit on $Y_1$, $Y_2$. The paper itself says that the class $\mathcal P$ of the source lists fewer conditions than it uses. I found no error in the estimates that the paper proves after Proposition 2.1, so the result is correct if Proposition 2.1 is correct. Until these three parts are proved from the source's definitions, the abstract ("We disprove", "we construct") and Theorem 1.1 must state that the result depends on them.
